![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/96f465c4da3f2e482fa0224e23564d27e363a727602ec05ed6daad8213807211.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by ${x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}=5$ and $x=\sqrt{3},$ where $x\ge 0,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our first function in terms of $y,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}=5\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{5-2{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & =\sqrt{5-2{y}^{2}} \\ 3 & =5-2{y}^{2} \\ 2{y}^{2} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Hence, the limits of integration are from $y=-1$ to $y=1.$ 

Let's draw our horizontal arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/54fbb219933d282480f70d8f87cbb8225c126979c58a5be6faed0a98eaf97c51.png)

 

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $x=\sqrt{3},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $x=\sqrt{5-2{y}^{2}}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}({[\sqrt{5-2{y}^{2}}]}^{2}-{[\sqrt{3}]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}([5-2{y}^{2}]-3)\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(2-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
